newsitem.title: USA: Odwalla tests positive for E. coli.
newsitem.headline: Odwalla tests positive for E. coli.

text.p: Washington state health officials said on Monday that a sample of Odwalla Inc apple juice had tested positive for the E. coli O157:H7 bacteria.

The state officials said at a news conference that the U.S. Food and Drug Administraiton had found the positive sample in a 16-ounce apple juice container taken from the company's Tukwila, Washington, distribution center.
The sample had an Oct. 24 pull date, but federal officials warned customers not to drink any Odwalla unpasteurized apple juice, apple juice product, carrot juice or vegetable cocktail.
The Centers for Disease Control reported that 10 more cases of the bacterial poisoning were found in the western United States and British Columbia, bringing the total to 39 in the recent outbreak.
The latest count showed 19 cases in Washington state, 10 in California, four in Colorado and six in the Canadian province.
The company said on Monday it had completed its recall and was continuing to study the cause of the outbreak.
A FDA spokesman said pasteurization of fruit juice transported across state lines was one option being considered to prevent further outbreaks.
